options.content: **Developer tier.** Every panel below the Memory Context row needs the exporter started with `--include-engula-debug-metrics` (off by default). If panels are empty, check that flag before anything else.

panels.description: Server memory from Valkey's own accounting: `zmalloc` is everything allocated and `logic` subtracts what maxmemory does not count.
panels.title: Memory Used

panels.description: Arena memory Engula has identified as reclaimable but has not reclaimed yet.
panels.title: Memory Blocks

panels.description: Memory excluded from the maxmemory calculation — replication backlog, AOF buffers and client output buffers.
panels.title: Overhead

panels.description: How far logical memory usage sits above maxmemory, clamped at zero. Anything above zero is what eviction still has to recover.
panels.title: Memory To Free
Defrag Drivers
panels.description: The two signals that pace defragmentation. `Defrag` is the fragmentation signal — it is what compaction can actually act on. `Usage` is how close the instance is to maxmemory. Defrag work tracking `Usage` while `Defrag` sits at zero means passes are being driven by a condition compaction cannot fix: the memory is genuinely full, not fragmented.

panels.title: Eviction Triggers
panels.description: What forces an urgent defragmentation pass. The two urgent lines split by call site: `Timer` is evictionTimeProc's spin loop, `Recycle` is the engula_mem_recycle branch at the tail of performEvictions. A timer tick can raise both.

panels.title: Tasks per Trigger
panels.description: Defragmentation tasks created per urgent trigger. One eviction pass can drive many task creations, so this is the amplification between the eviction path and the work it sets off.

panels.title: Reclaimable Memory
panels.description: `Recyclable` is memory identified as reclaimable but not reclaimed yet; `Recycling` is memory moving through reclamation. Both at zero while defrag runs hard means there is nothing left for it to recover — the arena is full rather than fragmented.

panels.title: Forecast Rates
panels.description: The forecast controller's own pacing state, not the instance's: `Inflow` and `Reclaim` are EWMAs rather than instantaneous rates, and all three read 0 while the forecast gate is shut — a flat zero here does not mean nothing is happening. `Target` is the reclaim rate it is steering towards.

panels.title: Time to Wall
panels.description: How long the controller projects until memory hits the wall. The server reports -1 while the forecast is inactive and the exporter drops negatives, so an inactive controller shows as a gap rather than as a value.

panels.title: Forecast Keys
panels.description: Keys the eviction forecaster has walked.

panels.title: Eviction Timer Active
panels.description: Whether the eviction timer is currently armed (1) or idle (0).

panels.title: Current Fill Rate
panels.description: Blocks grouped by how full they are, right now. Buckets are the arena's own fill-rate ranges (earena.h): coarse below 80%, then 1% wide up to 95%, and a [95%, 100%] catch-all that is never a defrag candidate. Weight in the low buckets is what defragmentation exists to compact.

panels.title: Fill Rate Over Time
panels.description: The same distribution over time, stacked. Weight migrating down towards the coarse low buckets is fragmentation building up; the reverse is defragmentation winning.

panels.title: Defrag Candidate Blocks
panels.description: Blocks split at the boundary defragmentation actually uses. earena_defrag_task_create() asserts the [95%, 100%] catch-all is never a candidate, so `Candidates` is the entire pool compaction may draw from. A candidate line pinned at zero while tasks are still being created means candidates are appearing and being consumed inside one scrape interval.

panels.title: Block Population
panels.description: Blocks the arena is still writing into (`Mutable`) against blocks sealed and queued for reclamation (`Recycling`).

panels.title: Task Creation
panels.description: Every call into task creation, and what came of it. `Threshold` is incremented when every bucket up to the cap is empty — there was nothing worth compacting; `Insufficient` is a claim truncated to a single block. The three outcomes sum to `Attempted`.

panels.title: Candidate Availability
panels.description: Share of attempts that found no candidate at all. Climbing towards 1.0 means the arena has run out of blocks worth compacting, and the attempts are pure overhead.

panels.title: Execution Path
panels.description: Where created tasks actually run. `Inline urgent` never enters the queue and executes on the main thread at creation; `Queued` is created minus inline urgent; `Inline main thread` is queued work the io threads did not drain, pulled back by a main-thread coroutine. All of the work sitting on `Inline urgent` means the async path is unused and every pass is on the request path.

panels.title: Queue Depth
panels.description: Work pending in the defrag queue and tasks accepted but not yet finished. Both flat at zero alongside a busy Execution Path confirms the queue is being bypassed rather than drained quickly.

panels.title: Blocks Retired vs Produced
panels.description: Blocks consumed and written back by completed tasks.

panels.title: Records Moved
panels.description: Records read out of retired blocks and written into new ones. The two should track each other — a lasting gap means records are being dropped or added along the way.

panels.title: Record Bytes Moved
panels.description: The same movement measured in bytes. `New` below `Old` is the space each pass squeezes out of the records it rewrites.

panels.title: Blocks per Task
panels.description: Blocks consumed and produced per completed defragmentation task. `After` staying well below `Before` is the compaction ratio each pass achieves.

panels.title: Defrag Yield
panels.description: Share of the bytes a pass moves that it actually recovers, as 1 − produced/retired. This is the return on the work: a low yield with a high task rate means compaction is rewriting memory for very little gain.

panels.title: Work vs Return
panels.description: Bytes moved per second against bytes recovered per second. The distance between the two lines is the cost of the compaction; they converge only when a pass is recovering nearly everything it touches.

panels.title: Task Accounting
panels.description: `Attempted − created − threshold − insufficient`. Every call into task creation ends in exactly one of the three outcomes, so this belongs at zero. A standing offset is a counting bug, not a workload change.

panels.title: Block Accounting
panels.description: Blocks claimed at creation minus blocks the completions report consuming. Every claimed block must reach a completion, so this belongs at zero; a growing gap means tasks are being dropped between claim and completion.

title: Engula Defragmentation
description: Developer-tier view of Engula's defragmentation: what drives it, whether there are candidates to act on, where the passes run, what they return, and two invariants that catch counting bugs. Requires the exporter to run with --include-engula-debug-metrics.
